text:
security-alert-bot: Alert — SSO token refresh spike detected: 75 distinct users, ~350 refresh requests, originating from 3 countries over 4 minutes. Possible token replay or credential stuffing. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/alerts/1781234567 :eyes:

amanda: seeing that on the auth dashboard as well. Most hits to /oauth/refresh and a bunch of 401s then lockouts.

raj: we've got 12 user lockouts and 4 service-account throttles. Logs show repeated refresh_token usage for same sub within secs.

linda: that pattern looks like refresh-token replay — mobile app may be leaking refresh tokens or a token db was scraped. Any recent RBAC or KMS changes?

sam: no RBAC changes this week from infra. KMS had a key rotation job scheduled but it failed on 03/16 (infra alert). Could be related if tokens were re-signed incorrectly, but replay doesn't need KMS.

maria: rotating the signing key is possible w/ KMS key versioning with no downtime, but we need to push new public key to our OIDC jwks endpoint and brief TTL handling in clients. Not instantaneous for mobile.

karen: containment steps proposed so far: 1) revoke refresh tokens for affected users, 2) temporarily raise MFA prompts/rate-limit on /oauth/refresh, 3) block suspicious IP ranges at Cloud WAF, 4) preserve full audit logs. Agree? :+1:

raj: agree. I'm running mass-revoke for the 75 users now. Curl snippet I'm using:```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://auth.internal/api/v1/sessions/revoke_batch \
  -d '{"user_ids": ["u123","u456",...], "revoke_refresh": true}'
```

amanda: temporarily increasing rate-limit on /oauth/refresh to 5/min per IP and 20/min per client-id. Will flip in edge config and monitor.

linda: capture and export the auth logs before we rotate anything. I've kicked off an export to secure S3 bucket: s3://incidents/1781234567/auth-logs-raw.tar.gz

sam: question on KMS: if we rotate the signing key, do we also need to rotate the access token validation window to avoid rejecting legit sessions? Maria?

maria: yes — plan: publish new jwks key version, set short overlap window (5m) for acceptance of old signatures, then revoke refresh tokens. That reduces user impact. For mobile clients with long-lived access, revoking refresh tokens forces a reauth.

oncall: tagging this as sev2 for now. Creating incident ticket: INC-2026-342 and assigning to eng-security + auth-oncall.

karen: we should also check for RBAC misconfig: any service principals that recently got expanded perms to read token DB?

raj: found two recent service tokens created by CI job 'mobile-release' on 03/15 with read:tokens permission. I've rotated those service tokens and removed read:tokens. Sending audit of who used them.

amanda: adding a temporary rule to reject refresh requests with UA headers matching the suspicious batch (old Android/okhttp pattern). Might cut noise.

linda: forensic notes: preserve DB snapshots (auth.tokens table) and the KMS key metadata. Also flag all accounts that had >3 refresh attempts in 1 minute as 'suspicious' for follow-up.

sam: post-incident actions we should track: 1) add replay-detection heuristics (reuse within short TTL), 2) enforce shorter refresh token lifetime for mobile (e.g., 7 days), 3) tighten service principal RBAC for token reads, 4) run appsec review for mobile SDK.

maria: I'll create a runbook update for key rotation to include jwks publish steps and overlap window config. Also adding a checklist to the incident doc for KMS rotation verification.

oncall: communications: external CSM + security customers? We should notify enterprise customers with affected sessions — draft notice ready in #customer-security-drafts. Internal exec note for legal is queued.

karen: one more ask — keep an eye on MFA fatigue risks: if we trigger mass reauth, support will get a lot of tickets. Ops to enable bypass codes for SRE troubleshooting only.

raj: mass-revoke finished for initial set. Follow-up query to find next wave:```sql
SELECT user_id, count(*) as attempts
FROM `auth.logs.refresh_attempts`
WHERE timestamp > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 24 HOUR)
GROUP BY user_id
HAVING attempts > 10
ORDER BY attempts DESC
```

amanda: dashboards updated. Incoming traffic dropped ~70% after WAF rules + UA block. Still seeing a low-level tail.

linda: preserving chain of custody: snapshot S3 export SHA256: abc123... and added to INC-2026-342.

sam: assigning owners: maria -> KMS/key rotation runbook + jwks, raj -> token DB RBAC & forensic queries, amanda -> WAF/rate-limits and dashboards, karen -> customer comms and support playbook.

oncall: great. We'll reconvene in 30m to validate containment and decide on broader rotate. If anything critical happens ping @oncall directly. :lock:

security-alert-bot: Alert resolved (contained) — suspicious activity dropped to baseline. Incident INC-2026-342 active for postmortem.

karen: thanks all. Postmortem owners — please target draft by EOD tomorrow and include metric impact (auth latency, support tickets, token revokes).

maria: got it. I'll include migration notes for clients and a timeline for key rotation.

raj: uploading final forensic artifacts to the incident folder now.

amanda: will follow up with recommended default rate-limit changes and a new alert for refresh spikes >50/min.

linda: adding replay-detection unit tests to auth service backlog.

oncall: closing thread for now. Thanks everyone.
